understanding: The task aims to harden the existing covered-after-restart recovery mechanism to eliminate false-FAILED statuses on completed and committed tasks, specifically addressing an incident where 9 restarts caused verified code tasks to incorrectly fail. The solution introduces a fail-closed helper `Test-TaskCompletionRecoverable` in `lib/task-action-evidence.ps1`, uses identity-keyed `task_started_at` in `driver/81:1657`, and prepends `[task:<id>]` in auto-commits from `driver/83:265` before truncation. Recovery logic triggers on restart/cap-hit reconciliation (`driver/60:217`), covered-after-restart (`driver/86:1465`), and fast-path (`driver/81:1466`) BEFORE marking a task failed. Task identification uses exact-id-match, and completion verification uses a commit-relative AND-chain (qa_head==HEAD AND critic.ts>=commit_ts). The system remains fail-closed, and control-plane blast radius is mitigated via canary deployment, admission control, and rollback. No net-new subsystem is introduced; this strengthens FOUNDATION #2.
summary: Hardening covered-after-restart recovery by adding a fail-closed `Test-TaskCompletionRecoverable` helper, identity-keyed task tracking, and prepended task IDs in auto-commits, triggered before failure marking to prevent false-FAILED outcomes on completed tasks, with exact-id-match and commit-relative AND-chain verification to avoid false-DONE on template tasks.

decision_atoms.reason: Provides a dedicated, reusable function to verify task completion recoverability using exact-id-match and commit-relative AND-chain, centralizing the recovery logic and keeping it fail-closed.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds a new function to an existing library, requiring careful integration and testing, but avoids creating a new subsystem.

decision_atoms.reason: Ensures precise tracking of when a task started, enabling accurate comparison with commit timestamps (`critic.ts>=commit_ts`) to verify completion.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires storage and retrieval of an additional keyed value, slightly increasing state management complexity, but critical for exact recovery verification.

decision_atoms.statement: Prepend `[task:<id>]` in auto-commits from `driver/83:265` before truncation
decision_atoms.reason: Makes task identity explicitly visible in commit messages, facilitating exact-id-match during recovery without relying on text-based grep.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Slightly alters commit message format, which could affect external tools parsing commit messages, but the prefix is structured and non-invasive.

decision_atoms.statement: Trigger recovery logic BEFORE marking task failed in restart/cap-hit reconciliation (`driver/60:217`), covered-after-restart (`driver/86:1465`), and fast-path (`driver/81:1466`)
decision_atoms.reason: Ensures that completed tasks are recovered and not incorrectly marked FAILED, directly addressing the incident where verified code tasks failed after restarts.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds a check in multiple code paths, increasing execution time slightly, but prevents false-FAILED outcomes and reduces wasted re-processing.

decision_atoms.statement: Implement exact-id-match and commit-relative AND-chain (qa_head==HEAD AND critic.ts>=commit_ts) for completion verification
decision_atoms.reason: Prevents false-DONE on template tasks by ensuring the task ID matches exactly and the commit is relative to the task's start time, not just any matching text.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: More restrictive than a simple grep, potentially missing some edge cases, but fail-closed design ensures safety over completeness.

decision_atoms.statement: Mitigate control-plane blast radius with canary deployment, admission control, and rollback capabilities
decision_atoms.reason: Limits the impact of any unforeseen issues in the recovery logic, allowing gradual rollout and quick reversal if problems arise.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires additional deployment infrastructure and monitoring, but essential for a medium-risk change in a critical path.

assumptions: The existing covered-after-restart mechanism (FOUNDATION #2) is functional and well-understood.
The `task_started_at` timestamp is reliably recorded when a task begins execution.
Auto-commits in `driver/83:265` can be safely modified to include the `[task:<id>]` prefix without breaking other processes.
The `qa_head` and `critic.ts` values are accessible and accurate at the time of recovery checks.
Canary deployment and rollback procedures are already established or can be implemented without significant overhead.
The incident (SHA256: 9 restarts→failed on verified code) is representative of the class of false-FAILED issues to be addressed.

risks.risk: False-DONE on template tasks due to incorrect exact-id-match or timestamp comparison
risks.mitigation: Fail-closed design ensures that any uncertainty results in not recovering the task (leaving it as failed), and canary deployment with monitoring will detect any unexpected DONE markings.

risks.risk: Performance degradation from additional checks in restart/cap-hit paths
risks.mitigation: Optimize the `Test-TaskCompletionRecoverable` helper to minimize overhead, and monitor system metrics during canary phase to detect any significant slowdown.

risks.risk: Incorrect integration of `[task:<id>]` prefix breaking commit parsing or other tooling
risks.mitigation: Admission control and canary deployment will limit exposure; rollback plan is in place if parsing issues are detected.

risks.risk: State corruption or race conditions when storing/retrieving identity-keyed `task_started_at`
risks.mitigation: Use atomic write/read operations and validate data integrity; fail-closed behavior ensures tasks are not incorrectly recovered if state is inconsistent.

risks.risk: Recovery logic fails to trigger in all required paths, leaving some false-FAILED cases unresolved
risks.mitigation: Comprehensive testing with the 9-restart incident scenario and monitoring of outcome-ledger for 24 hours post-deployment to verify reduction in false-FAILED entries.

minimal_version: Implement `Test-TaskCompletionRecoverable` helper with exact-id-match and commit-relative AND-chain, integrate into `driver/60:217`, `driver/86:1465`, and `driver/81:1466` before failure marking, and add identity-keyed `task_started_at` in `driver/81:1657`.
advanced_version: Minimal version plus prepend `[task:<id>]` in auto-commits from `driver/83:265` before truncation, canary deployment with admission control, automated rollback triggers, and 24-hour outcome-ledger monitoring dashboard to track false-FAILED reduction and restart-idle-run metrics.
